read.sloLead: At the end of the unit, the students will be able to:
slos: Explain, with examples, that civilizations throughout history have systematically studied living things [e.g., the history of numbers from Sumerians and its development to the present Arabic system]
Describe the set of real numbers as a combination of rational and irrational numbers
Demonstrate and verify the properties of equality and inequality of real numbers
Apply laws of indices to simplify radical expressions
Apply concepts of real numbers to real-world problems (such as temperature, banking, measures of gain and loss, sources of income and expenditure)

headings.title: Combination of Rational and Irrational Numbers
Representation of Rational and Irrational Numbers on Number Line
Application of Real Numbers in Daily Life.

read.sloLead: At the end of the unit, the students will be able to:
slos: Express a number in scientific notation and vice versa.
Describe logarithm of a number
Differentiate between common and natural logarithm

headings.title: Conversion of Numbers from Ordinary Notation to Scientific Notation
Conversion of Numbers from Scientific Notation to Ordinary Notation
Finding Common Logarithm of a Number

read.sloLead: At the end of the unit, the students will be able to:
slos: Recall:
Describe mathematics as the study of patterns, structure, and relationships.
Identify sets and apply operations on three sets (Subsets, overlapping sets and disjoint sets), using Venn diagrams.
Solve problems on classification and cataloguing by using Venn diagrams for scenarios involving two sets and three sets. Further application of sets.
Verify and apply properties/laws of union and intersection of three sets through analytical and Venn diagram methods.
Apply concepts from set theory to real-world problems (such as in demographic classification, categorizing products in shopping malls)
Explain product, binary relations and its domain and range.
Recognize that a relation can be represented by a table, ordered pair and graphs.
Recognize notation and determine the value of a function and its domain and range.
Identify types of functions (into, onto, one-to-one, injective, surjective and bijective) by using Venn diagrams.

headings.title: Mathematics as the Study of Patterns, Structures and Relationships
Identification of Sets Using Venn Diagram
Relation as Table, Ordered Pair and Graphs
Function and its Domain and Range

read.notes: Section 3.2.2 heading 'Real-World Applications' appears numbered as 3.2.2 on page/image 17, which duplicates the earlier 3.2.2 'Operations on Three Sets' numbering on image 10 · this is printed as-is in the book, not corrected.

read.sloLead: At the end of the unit, the students will be able to:
slos: Identify common factors, trinomial factoring, concretely, pictorially and symbolically.

Factorize quadratic and cubic algebraic expressions:
a4 + a2b2 + b4 or a4 + b4
ax2 + bx + c
(x + a) (x + b) (x + c) (x + d) + k
a3 + 3a2b + 3ab2 + b3
a3 ± b3
x2 + px + q
(ax2 + bx + c) (ax2 + bx + d) + k
(x + a) (x + b) (x + c) (x + d) + kx2
a3 – 3a2b + 3ab2 – b3
Find highest common factor and least common multiple of algebraic expressions and know relationship of LCM and HCF.
Find square root of algebraic expression by factorization and division.
Apply the concepts of factorization of quadratic and cubic algebraic expression to real-world problems (such as engineering, physics, and finance.)

headings.title: Identifying Common Factors and Trinomials Concretely, Pictorially and Symbolically
Factorizing Quadratic and Cubic Algebraic Expressions
Highest Common Factor (HCF) and Least Common Multiple (LCM) of Algebraic Expressions
Square Root of an Algebraic Expression

read.notes: The Type – I, Type – II, Type – III, Type – IV, Type – V labels within section 4.1.3 (e.g. 'Type – I: Factorization of expression of the types...') are sub-labels rather than numbered headings, so they were not listed separately as headings, though their content is summarized under 4.1.3's SLO bullet list. Also SLO bullets are printed as a mix of two-column bullet lists across pages; the joining order shown reconstructs the original left/right column layout as best inferred from image 1.

read.sloLead: At the end of the unit, the students will be able to:
slos: Solve linear equations and inequalities with rational coefficients and represent the solution set on a real line.
Solve two linear inequalities with two unknowns simultaneously.
Interpret and identify regions in plane bounded by two linear inequalities in two unknowns.
Find maximum and minimum values of a function using points in the feasible solution.

headings.title: Solving a Linear Equation in One Variable
Solution of a Linear Inequality in Two Variables
Solution of Two Linear Inequalities in Two Variables
Maximum and Minimum Values of a Function in the Feasible Solution

read.notes: Section 5.3 appears to contain a subsection labelled 5.3.2 (Maximum and Minimum Values...) without a visible 5.3.1 heading printed anywhere in the provided pages; this is copied as printed.

read.sloLead: At the end of the unit, the students will be able to:
slos: Identify angles in standard positions expressed in degrees and radian.
Apply Pythagoras theorem and the sine, the cosine and tangent ratios for acute angles of a right angle.
Solve real life trigonometric problems in 2-D involving angles of elevation and depression
Prove the trigonometric identities and apply them to draw different trigonometric relations.
Solve real life problems involving trigonometric identities.

headings.title: Identifying Angles in Standard Position (Degrees and Radians)
Converting Degrees to Minutes and Seconds
Converting from Degrees, Minutes and Seconds to Decimal Degrees
Trigonometric Ratios of an Acute Angle
Values of Trigonometric Ratios of Special Angles
The Angle of Elevation and the Angle of Depression

read.sloLead: At the end of the unit, the students will be able to:
slos: Derive distance formula by locating the position of two points in coordinate plane.
Calculate the midpoint of a line segment.
Find the gradient of a straight line when coordinates of two points are given.
Find the equation of a straight line in the form y =mx +c.
Find the gradient of parallel and perpendicular lines.
Apply distance and midpoint formulas to solve real-life situations such as physical measurements or distances between locations.
Apply concepts from coordinate geometry to real world problems (such as, aviation and navigation, landscaping, map reading, longitude and latitude).
Derive equation of a straight line in: slope- intercept form, point-slope form, two-point form, intercepts form, symmetric form, normal form.
Show that a linear equation in two variables represents a straight line and reduce the general form of the equation of a straight line to the other standard forms.

headings.title: Slope or Gradient of a Straight Line Joining Two Points
Equation of a Straight Line Parallel to the x-axis (or perpendicular to the y-axis)
Equation of a straight Line Parallel to the y-axis (or perpendicular to the x-axis )
Standard Forms of Equation of Straight Line: Intercepts of a line
A Linear Equation in two Variables Represents a Straight Line
Transform the General Linear Equation to Standard Forms
Applications of Coordinate Geometry in Real life Situations

read.notes: Sub-forms 'Point-slope Form', 'Symmetric Form', 'Two-point Form', 'Intercept Form', 'Normal Form' under 7.2.4 are numbered as list items (2,3,4,5,6) without decimal section numbers, so not included separately as headings; they are captured within the bullet listing SLO for standard forms.

read.sloLead: At the end of the unit, the students will be able to:
slos: Understand a mathematical statement and its proof
Differentiate between an axiom, conjecture and theorem.
Formulate simple deductive proofs [algebraic proofs that require showing the LHS to be equal to the RHS. e.g., showing (x − 3)² + 5 = x² − 6x + 14]

headings.title: Explanation of the Use of the Symbols

read.sloLead: At the end of the unit, the students will be able to:
slos: Identify similarity of polygons. Area and volume of similar figures.
Solve problems using the relationship between areas of similar figures and volume of similar solids.
Solve real life problems that involve the properties of regular polygons, triangles and parallelograms (such as building architectural structures, fencing, tiling, painting and carpeting a room).

headings.title: Geometrical Properties of Polygon and their Applications

read.sloLead: At the end of the unit, the students will be able to:
slos: Recall sketch graphs of linear functions (e.g. y = ax + b)

Plot and interpret the graphs of quadratic, cubic, reciprocal and exponential functions.
Graph y = ax^n where n is +ve integer, –ve integer, rational number for x > 0 and a is any real number.
Graph y = ka^x, where x is real a > 1.
Discover exponential growth/decay of a practical phenomenon through its graph.
Determine the gradients of curves by drawing tangents.
Apply concepts of sketching and interpreting graphs to real-life problems (such as in tax payment, income and salary problems and cost and profit analysis)

headings.title: Graph of Exponential Functions (y = ka^x where x is real number, a > 1)
Graphs of y = ax^n (where n is +ve integer, –ve integer or rational number for x > 0 and a is any real number)
Exponential Growth / Decay of a Practical Phenomenon through its Graph
Gradients of Curves by Drawing Tangents

read.notes: The SLOs bullet 'Plot and interpret the graphs...' has two sub-bullet points included within it as printed under that main bullet.

read.sloLead: At the end of the unit, the students will be able to:
slos: Construct a triangle having given two sides and the included angle.
Construct a triangle having given one side and two of the angles.
Construct a triangle having given two of its sides and the angle opposite to one of them.
Draw angle bisectors, perpendicular bisectors, medians, altitudes of a given triangle and verify their concurrency.

Draw loci and intersection of loci for set of points in two dimensions which are
at a given distance from a given point.
at a given distance from a given line
equidistant from two given points
equidistant from two given intersecting lines
Solve real life problems using the loci and interesting loci.

headings.title: Perpendicular Bisectors and Medians of a Triangle

read.sloLead: At the end of the unit, the students will be able to:
slos: Construct a grouped frequency table, histogram (with unequal class interval) and frequency polygon.
Calculate the mean, modal class and median of a grouped frequency distribution.

Solve real life situations involving mean, weighted mean, median and mode for given data (such as allocation of funds in different projects, forecasting future demographics, marketing, forecasting government budgets).

headings.title: Real Life Situations Involving Mean, Weighted Mean, Median and Mode

read.notes: Section heading 'Formation of Frequency distribution' on image 3 and 'Method of finding Arithmetic Mean for Grouped Data' / 'Short Formula for Computing Arithmetic Mean' on images 13-14 and 'Median for Grouped Data' on image 16, 'Mode for Grouped Data' on image 19, 'Sales and Marketing' on image 21 are unnumbered sub-headings, not listed to keep only numbered ones per instructions; they are omitted.

read.sloLead: At the end of the unit, the students will be able to:
slos: Calculate the probability of a single event and the probability of an event not occurring.
Solve real life problems involving probability.
Calculate relative frequency as an estimate of probability.
Calculate expected frequencies.
Solve real life problems involving relative and expected frequencies.

headings.title: Probability of an Event Not Occurring
Relative Frequency as an Estimate of Probability
Real Life Application of Relative Frequency
Real Life Application on Expected Frequency
